escena: SCENE (Efeonce office, Santiago, high floor, late morning): a video-call background seen from the chair of someone sitting at the meeting table inside the Efeonce meeting room named «Responder.» — camera at SEATED EYE LEVEL (about 1.15 m), 28 mm lens at f/5.6, like a good webcam view, looking straight at the back wall 2.5 m away; horizon level, verticals straight. Image 1 is the final artwork of that back wall: a matte dark-navy wall with the room name «Responder» in large white letters and its blue sphere as the period, and a wall-mounted whiteboard with the handwritten question, a small handwritten header, the three handwritten tool names and their tally marks. Reproduce that artwork exactly, as real materials: the room name is cut matte white vinyl lettering applied flat on the wall and the sphere an azure vinyl dot, the one saturated azure accent of the room; the whiteboard is a real glossy enamel board with an aluminium frame and a marker tray; the writing is real dry-erase marker ink with slightly uneven strokes. The wall artwork occupies the RIGHT 55% of the frame. At the far right edge a floor-to-ceiling clear glass wall of the room opens onto the bright open office beyond, out of focus: pale oak desks, a current-generation borderless monitor with a blue screen glow, tall windows with the Andes far away in haze. LIGHT: hard, low late-morning sunlight enters from the right through that glass, crossing the room as crisp visible shafts and raking diagonally across the navy wall, so the edge of the beam catches the word «Responder» and part of the whiteboard while the rest of the wall falls into rich, detailed dark shade; no direct light reaches the left part of the frame. TRACES OF WORK: a mesh office chair pushed back at an angle from the oak table at the right, a black dry-erase marker with its cap off lying on the whiteboard tray, a current-generation thin laptop half-open on the table edge with its screen dark. Nothing else on the walls: no books, no plants inside the room, no posters, no clocks, no extra signage and no extra text anywhere. TEXT EXCEPTION: the wall artwork from Image 1 is the ONLY readable text in the picture and it stays crisp and fully legible, every word and every tally mark spelled and placed exactly as in the artwork, never blurred, never altered, never translated; every other screen or paper in the scene stays illegible by physical means.
